questions: What should happen if a type‑2 query is executed when the stack is empty?
Does the initial stack of 100 zero‑labeled cards count toward the maximum stack size, i.e., can the stack grow beyond 100 cards after pushes?
Are the initial 100 cards considered part of the stack for the purpose of removal, so that the first type‑2 query will output 0 if no pushes have occurred?
Must the program enforce that the integer x in a type‑1 query lies within the given range 1 ≤ x ≤ 100, or can out‑of‑range values be ignored or cause an error?
Should the output for each type‑2 query be printed on its own line without extra spaces or trailing whitespace?
Is there any requirement on the order of processing when multiple queries are given on the same line or with extra whitespace?
Will the input always conform to the described format (no missing values, no extra tokens), or should the solution handle malformed lines?
Are there any limits on the total number of cards that can be on the stack at any time, and if so, what should be done when that limit is exceeded?
answers: No. Under the constraints of this problem, the stack always has at least one card.

inline_prompts:
There is a stack of 100 cards, each labeled with the integer 0. Process Q queries. Each query is of one of the following:  
- Type 1: Place a card labeled with an integer x on top of the stack.  
- Type 2: Remove the top card of the stack and output the integer written on that removed card.  
Input  
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:  
Q  
\text{query}_1  
\text{query}_2  
\vdots  
\text{query}_Q  
The i-th query \text{query}_i starts with the query type c_i (1 or 2), followed by the integer x if c_i=1.  
That is, each query is in one of the following two formats:  
1 x  
2  
Output  
Let q be the number of queries with c_i=2. Print q lines.  
The j-th line (1 \le j \le q) should contain the answer to the j-th such query.  
Constraints  
- 1 \le Q \le 100  
- 1 \le x \le 100  
- There is at least one query of type 2.  
- All input values are integers.  
- Under the constraints of this problem, the stack always has at least one card.
